subject: Request: Nightly P1/P2 response coverage exemption and escalation matrix
messages:
From: Sonia Patel <sonia@nebula-analytics.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@nebula-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 29 Jun 2025 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Nightly P1/P2 response coverage exemption and escalation matrix

Hi Jonas,

We’re kicking off a DB migration this weekend that will mean a small maintenance window between 02:00-04:00 PDT on Sat/Sun. Our SREs expect a spike in alerts during snapshots and the downstream batch jobs.

To avoid accidental P1 escalations for noisy alerts, can Redwood approve a temporary exception to the P1/P2 response policy for the nightly migration window (2am-4am) for the next two weekends?

Proposed guardrails from our side:
- Nebula will classify post-migration alerts tagged "maintenance" as non-P1 unless they hit the new health-check threshold
- We’ll share a watchlist of impacted endpoints and a runbook (attached)
- We’ll have a Nebula on-call SRE available by phone for any coordination

We’d like to document the exception window and an explicit escalation matrix so both teams know when to wake someone and when to tolerate transient failures. I attached our migration plan.

Thanks,
Sonia
Sonia Patel
Head of Platform Engineering
Nebula Analytics
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Sonia Patel <sonia@nebula-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Jun 2025 20:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Nightly P1/P2 response coverage exemption and escalation matrix

Hi Sonia — thanks for the heads up and for the clear runbook. I reviewed the migration plan you attached. Quick summary of Redwood’s position and asks before we can approve an exception: 

1) We can offer a scoped temporary carve-out for the two windows you requested, limited to alerts with the "maintenance" tag and only for endpoints listed in your watchlist.
2) We need an explicit escalation matrix so our on-call knows exactly when to treat an alert as P1 despite the window (e.g., data-loss, failed leader election, auth failures). Please include concrete examples.
3) Redwood will require an on-call point-of-contact from Nebula reachable by phone during the window and a Slack channel for the operation.
4) We will enable an automated fallback: if the P1 rate exceeds 5 within any 15-minute window for the watchlisted endpoints, the carve-out auto-cancels and alerts will be escalated per our standard P1 flow.

Attached: a draft escalation matrix (escalation-matrix.xlsx) and a short template for the P1 examples. Marissa — can you review the auto-cancel threshold and confirm SRE/ops playbook compatibility? Ben — I’ll need a quick note from you on whether this affects our night-shift routing and any extra coverage cost. Laura — please confirm contract implications (SLA amendment or simple exception).

If we get your updated watchlist + examples by tomorrow EOD, we can approve the carve-out for this weekend.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Sonia Patel <sonia@nebula-analytics.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@nebula-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 01:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Nightly P1/P2 response coverage exemption and escalation matrix

Thanks Jonas — attaching the watchlist and concrete failure examples now (see attachment). We agree to the auto-cancel threshold you proposed.

Examples included as requested:
- Data-loss: any partial write that results in sequence ID mismatch across replicas
- Leader election: more than 2 leader reassigns in 5 minutes for a shard
- Auth failures: > 10% auth errors across production endpoints for 10 minutes

POC details:
- On-call SRE: Mark Rivera (mobile: +1-415-555-0199)
- Slack channel: #nebula-migration-redwood

We’re good to proceed if you formalize the exception and confirm the fallback routing.

—
Sonia
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Sonia Patel <sonia@nebula-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Nightly P1/P2 response coverage exemption and escalation matrix

Sonia — all set. We reviewed internally and approve a limited exception for the upcoming two weekend windows (2025-07-05/06 and 2025-07-12/13) between 02:00-04:00 PDT with the following final terms:

- Scope: only alerts for endpoints on the attached watchlist and explicitly tagged "maintenance" by Nebula.
- Exceptions: the three concrete example classes you provided will still be treated as P1 if thresholds are met (data-loss, leader election, auth failures).
- Auto-cancel: if >5 P1-class alerts occur within 15 minutes for watchlisted endpoints, Redwood will immediately cancel the carve-out and escalate per standard P1 procedure.
- Communication: Nebula will maintain the POC (Mark Rivera) reachable by phone and keep #nebula-migration-redwood open.
- Documentation: Laura will issue a one-off SLA amendment doc that records the temporary exception (no change to baseline SLA).

Marissa: please add the auto-cancel rule to the routing policy and confirm monitoring will send a head-up email to the on-call when we hit 3 P1-class alerts in a 15-minute window.
Ben: confirm whether there will be any incremental night-shift cost for Redwood to observability during the carve-out — if so we’ll agree to a short priced addendum.

Sonia — I’ve attached the signed exception matrix and our routing appendix. If anything changes for your migration plan, please notify us ASAP.

Thanks,
Jonas
